description: Storefront search. Runs with no model configured, so it is safe in CI. Every case is a shopper request plus the properties any acceptable answer must have.

cases.why: The plainest possible request. If ranking cannot do this, nothing else matters.

cases.query: street food tour in Hanoi Old Quarter
cases.why: The reported failure: a food question answered with boat trips and cycling. Scoped to the first screen, because a ranked list of twenty is allowed a weak tail — the top of the page is the claim.

cases.query: somewhere by the sea, not the mountains
cases.why: A stated exclusion is a hard constraint. Explaining which mountain trip is least mountainous is not an answer.
A budget is a promise. One over-priced card destroys trust in every other number on the page.

cases.query: highly rated experiences in Hoi An
cases.why: Filters are the one part of the UI a shopper can verify at a glance.
Duration is the constraint most often silently dropped when relevance is strong.
An explicit category is not a hint.
A sort control that ranking quietly overrides is a lie in the UI.
Same argument as price, and the case merchandising pins could plausibly break.

cases.query: gentle activity for a family with a toddler
cases.why: Party composition has to reach ranking, not just the price calculation.
Selling a Phu Quoc boat trip to someone in the mountains is the most expensive kind of irrelevance.
Garbage input must degrade to browsing, not error and not an empty page.
The first page load carries no query at all.
Late bookers filter on this and cannot recover from a wrong answer.
Specific vocabulary that exists in the catalogue should rank exactly.
